content: In the Level Six reading the moon is a metaphor for the level of speech, since speech is dependent, manifesting only through the speaker's light, as the moon shines by the sun's. The form of speech that persists and shows its effects is the written (raqamī), and the text says raqam is identical to qamar on the basis of the letters. The splitting of the moon is thus the emergence of primordial meaning from the written-textual form without the mediation of reflective thought, unlike the derivation of conventional meanings through artificial assignment.
refers_to_primary: Ibn Turka, R. Shaqq-i Qamar u Bayān-i Sāʿat
